name: λ-box commutes with Z-phases
summary: A λ-box and a Z(α) phase commute.
description:
Both the λ-box and the Z-phase are diagonal, so they commute. Together they represent $\mathrm{diag}(1, \lambda e^{i\alpha})$: every complex number is represented by a λ-box and a phase.

**Conventions.** The λ-box of Ng and Wang is the diagonal map $\mathrm{diag}(1, \lambda)$ with $\lambda \geq 0$ (a yellow box in their papers, a green box in the LICS'18 paper of Hadzihasanovic, Ng and Wang). It is the same as a Z-box of arity 2 with label $\lambda$, which is how it is drawn and checked here (the rule holds for every complex $\lambda$; it is checked for some positive values). Scalars that the papers write as diagrams are given here as numbers.
